subject: SLO Bridging Plan: p95/p99 end-to-end latency reconciliation (hosted vs incumbent)
messages:
From: Tom Hall <tom.hall@veridian.ai>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, camila_reyes@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2025-06-18T14:02:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo: raw traces and p95/p99 targets

Hi Karthik / Camila,

Thanks for the demo today — good session. Quick summary of what we need from an end-to-end SLO perspective (edge -> app -> model):
- p95 <= 200 ms (overall response completion)
- p99 <= 450 ms (we need tight tail controls)
- sustained concurrency target: ~1,500 concurrent requests at peak traffic
- streaming: chunked responses where per-chunk emission latency ideally < 20 ms
- typical request: ~220 tokens (avg); 95th pct request size ~1,100 tokens

Current provider behavior: during several bursts we observed p99 spikes > 1.2s and token emission stalls in streaming. We uploaded a set of raw traces and spans to the shared Drive (perf-traces.zip) plus a short trace CSV that highlights three representative spikes (trace-summary.csv).

Ask: can Redwood run a hosted canary that mirrors our traffic envelope and return:
- side-by-side p95/p99 numbers for the same traffic window (hosted vs incumbent)
- token emission timing per-chunk for streaming paths
- an outline of failure modes and fallback behavior under congestion (what model variants or region fallbacks you would use)

We prefer a non-prod canary first. Also need a rollback / throttling plan and expected timelines.

Tom
Head of Platform Engineering
Veridian AI

Attachments: perf-traces.zip (zip), trace-summary.csv (csv)

From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Tom Hall <tom.hall@veridian.ai>
Cc: camila_reyes@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2025-06-18T17:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: raw traces and p95/p99 targets

Tom — thanks for the clear summary and for sharing the traces. Internal notes and proposed next steps below.

Summary of what we will validate (hosted API compare against incumbent):
- End-to-end p95 / p99 for the supplied traffic envelope (we will exercise both request/response and streaming flows)
- Per-chunk emission timing for streaming responses (we will capture token emission latencies)
- Concurrency shaping to approximate 1,500 concurrent active requests (we'll run progressive ramps)
- Behavior under sudden burst/shock and cold-cache vs warmed KV cache runs

Requested artifacts from your side (things we need to run an accurate comparison):
1) 1-minute traffic envelope (timestamps + qps shape) — raw CSV or proto traces (you already attached some, thanks).
2) Representative sample payloads (json) across 50/90/95/99 pct sizes.
3) Any edge-to-app hop latency budget (if you have CDN/edge timing separated).

Our plan and proposed schedule:
- 2025-06-19: You share final payload samples + confirm the Drive folder (we'll pull traces).
- 2025-06-20 to 2025-06-21: Redwood runs a 48-hour hosted synthetic test (mirrored envelope) + one-hour focused stress window to capture tails.
- 2025-06-23: Internal analysis and artifact delivery (p95/p99 tables, per-chunk traces, and tail event snapshots).
- 2025-06-24: Joint sync (30–45 min) to review results and discuss canary cutover / rollback criteria.

Ownership: camila_reyes will lead the SLO probe execution; marissa_cole will handle canary playbook and rollback policies. I will support procurement/contract questions if the hosted numbers look good.

Attachments: sla-qualification-matrix.xlsx (xlsx) — contains test matrix and measurement definitions.

If that timing works, Camila will kick off. We will ensure the hosted runs are in the us-west region unless you request otherwise.

—Karthik
Principal Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

> On 2025-06-18 14:02, Tom Hall wrote:
> > Thanks for the demo today — good session. Quick summary of what we need ...

From: Tom Hall <tom.hall@veridian.ai>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, camila_reyes@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2025-06-18T18:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: raw traces and p95/p99 targets

Karthik / Camila,

Appreciate the fast turnaround. I've uploaded the additional artifacts to the Drive folder and gave your team Editor access: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/0BxyzVeridianPerf
Files added: payload-samples.json (50/90/95/99), 1min-envelope.csv, perf-traces.zip (already there).

One clarification: when we say end-to-end, we mean edge (Fastly) -> app layer (our API) -> model service. CDN adds ~12–20 ms median; our target numbers above assume we include edge hops. Please include that span in the comparison.

We definitely want the canary to validate model-variant fallback behavior — during prior incidents the incumbent switched to a lower-qual variant and token emission spacing degraded significantly. Please include a canary test that exercises a fallback path (e.g., quantized variant) and document observable signature so we can automate rollback.

Tom
Head of Platform Engineering, Veridian AI

Link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/0BxyzVeridianPerf

From: camila_reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
To: Tom Hall <tom.hall@veridian.ai>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2025-06-19T09:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: raw traces and p95/p99 targets

Tom — thanks for uploading everything and for the edge clarification. Quick clarifying questions and a lightweight checklist so we don't miss anything before we start test execution: 

1) Confirmed: we will include Fastly -> app -> model spans in the E2E numbers. Please let us know if you want us to also run an isolated model-only test (app -> model) for kernel-level debugging.
2) Can you confirm the percent of streaming vs non-streaming calls in your peak window? We saw a mix but need an exact ratio to shape the test.
3) Please provide one example failing-span from the trace-summary.csv that you consider a p99 incident (we'll use it as a regression anchor).

Checklist we will complete before the joint sync:
- Pull traces + sample payloads (today 6/19)
- Baseline hosted run (48 hrs) in us-west (6/20–6/21)
- Warm-cache vs cold-cache runs and a fallback/quantized-variant exercise
- Deliver artifacts + measurement spreadsheet (6/23)
- Joint review (6/24) — calendar invite to follow

Attachments: payload-sample.json (json) — small sample of the payload types we will use for instrumentation.

Camila Reyes
SRE, Redwood Inference
camila_reyes@redwood.com
